clue.text: Without notice, alter fitting

indicators.note: without tells us to remove the following piece from the word for alter

parts.note: to alter is to adjust
AD is short for advertisement, a public notice

explanation.surface: Someone changes an attachment or fixture abruptly, giving no warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' removes AD from ADJUST, leaving the answer; 'fitting' looks like a noun but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something just is right and proper, which is one sense of fitting as an adjective.

clue.text: Jill's friend caught leaving appetisers for mischievous child

parts.note: Jack and Jill go up the hill together in the nursery rhyme

indicators.note: leaving says the abbreviation for caught departs from the snacks word

parts.note: canapes are small savoury appetisers
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: From the nursery rhyme, Jack is caught walking off from the party nibbles.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackanapes is a cheeky, impertinent person, often a naughty or pert child.

clue.text: Priest cuts shin up with large knife

indicators.note: cuts means the priest abbreviation slices into the climbing word

parts.note: to shin up is to climb, or scale

explanation.surface: A cleric wounds someone's leg with a big blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shin' looks like the leg but 'shin up' is to climb, SCALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalpel is a small, very sharp surgical knife.

clue.text: Charm ebbed unexpectedly in sleeping quarters

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters of charm ebbed turn up in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: A spell or allure fades without warning, somewhere in the bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges CHARM EBBED.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedchamber is an old word for a bedroom, the room where a person sleeps.

clue.text: Unrefined cycling centre unknown

indicators.note: cycling moves the front letter of the centre word round to the back

parts.note: the heart of something is its centre
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A rough, unpolished cycling hub of unknown location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the H of HEART to the end, giving EARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour or manners are coarse and down-to-earth, lacking refinement.

clue.text: Range of political blocs announced

indicators.note: announced tells us the answer is said like the word for political blocs

parts.note: caucuses are groups within a party or legislature

explanation.surface: A selection of party factions is made public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like a selection but is a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caucasus is the mountain range between the Black and Caspian Seas.

clue.text: I'm surprised captain with prosthetic leg has no foot

indicators.note: foot is the bottom of a down answer, so the captain's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Captain Ahab in Moby-Dick has a leg made of whale bone

explanation.surface: A sea captain with an artificial leg turns out to be missing a foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' seems literal, given the leg, but means the last letter in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Aha is an exclamation of surprise or sudden discovery.

clue.text: British businessman in a pickle, short of time

indicators.note: short of means the pickle name lacks the time abbreviation

parts.note: Branston is a well-known British brand of chutney-style pickle

explanation.surface: A British entrepreneur is in trouble and running out of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a pickle' reads as in trouble; 'in' is a link and the pickle is BRANSTON, a British brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Branson founded the Virgin group and is one of Britain's best-known entrepreneurs.

clue.text: Smack in Staffordshire town changing hands

indicators.note: the left hand is swapped for the right, so one hand abbreviation replaces the other

parts.note: Leek is a market town in Staffordshire, England

explanation.surface: Drugs are bought and sold in a small English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' looks like heroin but is the verb, as in 'smack of'; L (left) becomes R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: To smack of something is to carry a strong suggestion of it, much as to reek of it.

clue.text: Bullied and denied more shifts

indicators.note: shifts suggests the letters of denied more are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A worker was pushed around and refused extra hours of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' looks like work periods but rearranges DENIED MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To domineer is to rule arrogantly over others, so the past form means bullied.

clue.text: Angry demand of shellfish gatherer heard

indicators.note: heard tells us the answer is said like the word for a shellfish gatherer

parts.note: someone who digs for clams is a clammer

explanation.surface: A shellfish forager is overheard making a furious demand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' signals that CLAMMER, a clam digger, is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamour is a loud, insistent outcry, a vehement public protest or demand.

clue.text: Oblivious of finely-crafted work by Stubbs?

indicators.note: by means placed beside, here with the work coming after its maker's name

parts.note: Una Stubbs was an English actress; the question mark flags her first name standing for the surname
ware means manufactured goods, especially pottery or crafted wares

explanation.surface: It sounds like a question about a delicate piece by the painter George Stubbs.
explanation.walkthrough: Stubbs suggests George Stubbs, the horse painter, but it is the British actress Una Stubbs (Till Death Us Do Part, Sherlock); the question mark flags a first name standing in for its surname.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unaware of something is to have no knowledge of it, to be oblivious of it.

clue.text: Current measures to protect the earth I designed for combatting areas with crowds

indicators.note: to protect means the outer word wraps around and shields the remaining letters

parts.note: amps (amperes) are units measuring electric current

indicators.note: designed suggests the letters of the earth I are rearranged into a new plan

explanation.surface: Electrical units are built to safeguard the planet, as if for an environmental project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' looks like part of an engineering story but is the anagram signal; 'to protect' makes the current units wrap round the result. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman amphitheatres staged gladiatorial fights before tiers of spectators, so they were arenas for combat watched by crowds.

clue.text: Thug wanting bit of attention admitting twisting Trump's slogan, wretched child

indicators.note: admitting means the thug word lets the reversed slogan in
wanting means the thug word lacks the letter that follows

parts.note: a ruffian is a violent thug

indicators.note: bit of picks the first letter of attention
twisting means the slogan's letters are turned round

parts.note: MAGA is Make America Great Again

explanation.surface: A violent man craves notice while repeating a political slogan about a miserable youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' and 'bit of' strip one A from the thug; 'twisting' turns the slogan round, and 'admitting' sets it just after the opening R.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragamuffin is a dirty, ragged child, an urchin in tatters.

clue.text: Made responsive broadcast claiming "Settle is close to Carlisle"

indicators.note: claiming means the broadcast word takes the other pieces into itself

parts.note: to send a signal is to broadcast it
to sit is to settle, as a bird does

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of Carlisle

explanation.surface: A radio report asserts that Settle is near Carlisle; both lie on a northern English railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: Settle looks like the town at the start of the Settle–Carlisle railway, but it is the verb, SIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To sensitise is to make something reactive or more aware, so sensitised means rendered responsive.

clue.text: Fools with missing friends

indicators.note: missing says the abbreviation for with is absent from the word for fools

parts.note: a wally is British slang for a silly person

explanation.surface: Idiots have nobody beside them, deserted by their mates.
explanation.walkthrough: WALLY is British slang for a fool; 'missing' removes W (with) from WALLIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Allies are those who side with and support you, close in sense to friends.

clue.text: Spice is new dope inhaled by Deep Purple?

indicators.note: inhaled by means the following letters are drawn inside the colour word

parts.note: puce is a dark purplish-brown colour; the question mark admits it is an example
gen is British slang for information, as is dope

explanation.surface: A rock band, Deep Purple, has something fresh to smoke, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Deep Purple suggests the rock band but is the colour PUCE; GEN is British slang for information, like 'dope'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungence is sharpness or piquancy, the quality that gives food or remarks spice.

clue.text: Most expensive ways to hold sword up

indicators.note: to hold means the ways enclose the reversed weapon

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way; two of them for the plural

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the sword is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: Pricey methods for keeping a blade raised.
explanation.walkthrough: ST twice supplies the plural 'ways'; 'up' turns EPEE to EEPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep is informal for overpriced, so the steepest price is the highest.

clue.text: Relocate German in Abu Dhabi, perhaps

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for German inside the state name

parts.note: Abu Dhabi is one of the United Arab Emirates, an example of an emirate

explanation.surface: A German moves to make a new life in the Gulf.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's country to settle elsewhere, a permanent relocation abroad.

clue.text: One takes in Canadian singer's claim to be short of energy

indicators.note: to be short of means the claim loses the energy abbreviation

parts.note: the Canadian pop singer Justin Bieber would say I'm Bieber
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone is fooled by a tired pop star insisting on who he is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes in' looks like deceives but means swallows, as a drinker does.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbiber is a drinker, one who takes liquid in.

clue.text: Hams it up as English test is in Spanish

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British vehicles
es is the Spanish for is

explanation.surface: An English exam on display is set in the Spanish language.
explanation.walkthrough: MOT is the yearly safety test that cars in Britain must pass.
explanation.definitionFit: To emote is to act with exaggerated feeling, which is what an actor hamming it up does.

clue.text: Perform wearing hat, being touchy?

indicators.note: wearing means the hat goes around the performing word

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat
to act is to perform

explanation.surface: An actor must go on stage in a hat and is sensitive about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touchy' suggests irritable; the question mark flags the literal sense, to do with touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactile means relating to the sense of touch, a playful reading of touchy.

clue.text: Be next to a judge overwhelmed by murder

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the judge abbreviation is buried inside the murder phrase

parts.note: to do in is to murder

explanation.surface: Sitting beside a judge who is swamped by a murder case.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that adjoin are adjacent, sharing a boundary.

clue.text: Move by Tory leader, jerk, if journalist recalled financial shortfall

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of the party word
recalled means called back, so these pieces are read from the end

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary jerk
ED is short for editor, a senior journalist

explanation.surface: A Conservative chief makes a political move, with a reporter dredging up a past twitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses TIC IF ED into DEFICIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A budget deficit is when government spending exceeds income, leaving a gap in the public finances.

clue.text: Fight roughly, the first to be thrown out

indicators.text: the first to be thrown out
indicators.note: throwing out the first means the word for roughly loses its opening letter

parts.note: about means roughly, approximately

explanation.surface: A rough brawl in which the first man is ejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' seems to describe the fight but means ABOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bout is a contest, as in a boxing or wrestling match.

clue.text: Angry young man rings most of island

parts.note: O looks like a ring, so rings are Os

indicators.note: most of means the island's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Borneo is a large island in South-East Asia

explanation.surface: A furious youth telephones a big chunk of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' looks like a verb (phones) but is plural O shapes; 'most of' drops the last O of BORNEO.
explanation.definitionFit: John Osborne, author of Look Back in Anger, was the leading figure of the 1950s Angry Young Men writers.

clue.text: Seafood that's line caught

indicators.note: caught as in caught by the ear, heard, so the answer is said like the line word

parts.note: a row is a line

explanation.surface: Fish that was caught on a line rather than netted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line caught' reads as angling, but 'caught' means heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe is fish eggs, eaten as seafood such as caviar.

clue.text: Drugs work: 101 Dalmatians content to be released

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
the digits 1, 0, 1 resemble the letters I, O, I

indicators.note: letting the contents go leaves only the outer letters of the dog breed

explanation.surface: A job on the film 101 Dalmatians, with the dogs happy to be let out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' reads as happy but means the inside; 'to be released' empties DALMATIANS to DS.
explanation.definitionFit: Opioids are a class of painkilling drugs such as morphine and fentanyl.

clue.text: Product, primarily, in nut tree fluid

definitions.text: Product, primarily, in nut tree fluid

indicators.note: fluid means not fixed in form, so the letters flow into a new order
primarily picks out the first letter of product

explanation.surface: Something made from the sap of a tree, sold as a liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluid' rearranges P (first of 'Product') with IN NUT TREE; read whole, the clue describes the answer, a fluid produced from trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpentine is a volatile oil distilled from pine and terebinth tree resin, a tree product sold as a fluid.

clue.text: Nearly prepared to deliver

indicators.note: nearly means the word for prepared stops just short of its end

parts.note: ready means prepared

explanation.surface: Someone is almost set to hand something over.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a speech, lesson or statement aloud is to deliver it to an audience.
